Corn Cercospora leaf spot Gray leaf spot.cause: Caused by the fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis.
Corn Cercospora leaf spot Gray leaf spot.symptoms: Long rectangular gray or tan lesions on leaves that reduce photosynthesis.
Corn Cercospora leaf spot Gray leaf spot.dosage: Follow the manufacturer's label. Do not exceed the recommended rate.
Corn Cercospora leaf spot Gray leaf spot.treatment: Spray a recommended fungicide at the early stage of infection and repeat according to the product label.
Corn Cercospora leaf spot Gray leaf spot.prevention: Use resistant varieties, rotate crops, destroy infected crop residue, and avoid continuous maize cultivation.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors warm nights, high humidity, and extended leaf wetness — especially in continuous corn or reduced-tillage fields.

Corn Common rust.cause: Caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi.
Corn Common rust.symptoms: Small reddish-brown pustules on both sides of the leaves.
Corn Common rust.treatment: Apply fungicide at the first appearance of symptoms.
Corn Common rust.prevention: Use resistant hybrids and remove infected plant debris.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors cool, moist conditions with heavy dew. Spores spread further under windy conditions.

Corn Northern Leaf Blight.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped gray-green lesions on leaves.
Corn Northern Leaf Blight.treatment: Spray fungicide when disease is first noticed.
Corn Northern Leaf Blight.prevention: Crop rotation and resistant maize varieties.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors moderate temperatures with extended (6+ hour) periods of leaf wetness.

Tomato Bacterial spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruits.
Tomato Bacterial spot.treatment: Spray copper-based bactericide at early infection.
Tomato Bacterial spot.prevention: Use certified seed and avoid working with wet plants.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors warm, wet weather. Spreads via splashing or wind-driven rain, often worse after storms.

Tomato Early blight.symptoms: Brown concentric rings on older leaves.
Tomato Early blight.treatment: Spray fungicide immediately after symptoms appear.
Tomato Early blight.prevention: Rotate crops and remove infected leaves.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors warm weather with alternating wet and dry periods, often on older or stressed plants.

Tomato Late blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions with white mold underneath leaves.
Tomato Late blight.treatment: Spray immediately and repeat according to the product label.
Tomato Late blight.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and destroy infected plants.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors cool, wet, overcast weather — classic 'late blight weather'. Can devastate a crop within days once established.

Tomato Leaf Mold.symptoms: Yellow spots on upper leaves with olive-green mold underneath.
Tomato Leaf Mold.treatment: Apply fungicide and improve greenhouse ventilation.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors high humidity and moderate temperatures, especially in greenhouses or densely spaced plants with poor airflow.

Tomato Septoria leaf spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with gray centers and dark margins.
Tomato Septoria leaf spot.treatment: Spray fungicide and remove infected foliage.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors warm, wet conditions. Spores spread by splashing rain or overhead irrigation.

Tomato Spider mites Two spotted spider m.symptoms: Tiny yellow speckles, leaf bronzing, and webbing.
Tomato Spider mites Two spotted spider m.treatment: Apply miticide at the first sign of infestation.
Tomato Spider mites Two spotted spider m.prevention: Monitor crops regularly and control weeds.

weatherRisk.notes: Unlike fungal diseases, mites thrive in HOT, DRY conditions — risk rises as humidity drops, not as it rises.

Tomato Target Spot.symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings.
Tomato Target Spot.treatment: Apply fungicide according to label directions.
Tomato Target Spot.prevention: Improve air circulation and avoid excessive irrigation.

weatherRisk.notes: Favors warm, humid conditions with extended leaf wetness.

Tomato Tomato YellowLeaf Curl Virus.symptoms: Yellow curled leaves and stunted growth.
Tomato Tomato YellowLeaf Curl Virus.treatment: Control whiteflies immediately and remove infected plants.
Tomato Tomato YellowLeaf Curl Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties and insect-proof nets.

weatherRisk.notes: Spread by whiteflies, whose populations explode in hot, dry weather. Humidity itself isn't the driver — whitefly activity is.

Tomato Tomato mosaic virus.cause: Viral infection spread by contaminated tools and handling.
Tomato Tomato mosaic virus.symptoms: Mosaic leaf patterns, distortion, and reduced yield.
Tomato Tomato mosaic virus.treatment: Remove infected plants immediately and disinfect tools.
Tomato Tomato mosaic virus.prevention: Use certified seed and practice strict sanitation.

weatherRisk.notes: Spreads mainly through contaminated hands, tools, and plant-to-plant contact rather than weather conditions. Sanitation matters far more here than forecast.

Tomato healthy.symptoms: Healthy green leaves and vigorous growth.
